descriptionChirho: Denotes the mode, fashion, or manner in which something is done, most commonly appearing in the comparative construction ὃν τρόπον ('in the manner that' / 'just as'). All four auto-clustered senses share the same core meaning: Arabic طَريقَة (manner/method), Hindi तरह/प्रकार/रीति (way/manner), Hebrew דֶּרֶךְ/אֹפֶן (way/manner), Korean 방식/방법 (method/way), Spanish modo/manera (manner/way). Sense 77915 (Heb 13:5 'manner of life') shows a slight specialization toward 'character/conduct' (Arabic سُلُوك, Hindi आचरण) but this is a contextual coloring of the same basic lexical meaning rather than a genuinely distinct sense. The word consistently describes how something happens or is carried out, whether in similes (Matt 23:37, Luke 13:34, Acts 1:11, 7:28), general statements about manner (Acts 15:11, 27:25, Phil 1:18, 2 Tim 3:8), or the character of one's lifestyle (Heb 13:5).
